text:
**NVIDIA Is a Bubble in the Making — And It’s Going to Pop**

Let’s cut through the noise. NVIDIA isn’t just overvalued — it’s a full-blown speculative mania, trading on pure momentum and collective delusion. The numbers don’t lie. The P/E ratio is north of 90. For a company that’s not even a pure-play AI business, but rather a semiconductor finagler riding a hype wave, that’s not valuation — it’s surrender.

Did you know that more than 60% of NVIDIA’s revenue comes from just three hyperscalers? Microsoft, Amazon, and Google aren’t just customers — they’re hostages in a system built on Nvidia’s dominance. And that dominance is crumbling under the weight of its own arrogance. AMD is aggressively rolling out its MI300 series with better price-performance, and every major cloud provider is now investing heavily in custom AI accelerators. Google’s TPU v5, Amazon’s Trainium, Microsoft’s Maia — the dream of upward cloud infrastructure lock-in is already dead. The future isn’t Nvidia. It’s fragmentation.

You can’t have a three-billion-dollar market cap built on a single product cycle. You can’t justify supernormal growth when the initial use case — LLM inference — is already trending toward optimization, pruning, and distillation. The real demand isn’t for raw compute, it’s for efficient, cost-effective intelligence. And Nvidia is eating its own dog food in the most dangerous way: by making everyone believe they need more and more chips to keep up with AI.

This isn’t innovation. It’s financial theater.

The dot-com crash wasn’t because the internet wasn’t real. It was because companies were valued based on hype, not revenue, margins, or sustainable business models. Sound familiar? Skepticism isn’t guilt — it’s discipline. And right now, most investors are too afraid to be skeptical.

Look at the earnings: they’re strong, yes. But the narrative is permeating the market so deeply that retail traders are buying calls like they’re lottery tickets. The stock has gone from “moon” to “crash” with all the subtlety of a fueled-up freight train. And when history repeats, being on the wrong side of belief isn’t just painful — it’s terminal.

NVIDIA’s executives, especially Jensen Huang, are selling a future where every device, every home, every car runs AI. That future is not now — and it never will be, unless demand materializes at a scale that actually makes sense. But no one is really auditing the math. Because the math says we’re already past peak demand for GPU-heavy training.

Price is not value. High growth isn’t sustainable. And when the juggernaut slows — and it will — the drop won’t be gradual. It will be violent. The delusion will collapse in a single quarter. And people will wake up the next day wondering how they missed the signal.

The math is simple: too many dollars, too little demand. Too much confidence, too little substance. The bubble isn’t just inflating — it’s already bursting.

And you? You’re still buying at the top.

**NVIDIA’s P/E Ratio Is a Blood Moon Over a Digital Boomtown**

Let’s be brutally honest: NVIDIA’s current valuation isn’t just high—it’s obscene. A price-to-earnings ratio hovering near 70, with forward P/E stretching toward 100, isn’t a number for a company; it’s a whisper from the abyss. And it’s screaming one word: *crisis*. 

Compare that to Cisco in 1999—the absolute peak of the dot-com mania—and you’ll find a chilling parallel. Cisco peaked with a P/E of around 140, a time when the internet was still a novelty and the business model was built on hope, not revenue. Today, NVIDIA trades at a P/E that’s not *much lower*, despite being a company with real earnings—albeit driven almost entirely by a single, volatile trend: AI. 

This isn’t innovation. This is a self-sustaining feedback loop of hype. Investors are buying NVIDIA not because it’s cheap or fundamentally sound, but because they believe someone else will pay *more* tomorrow. It’s the greater-fool theory parading as investment strategy, dressed up as “the future of computing.” But futures are not guaranteed. 

Let’s get real about the risks:  
• Revenue is concentrated in a handful of hyperscalers—Amazon, Microsoft, Google—whose AI spending is already showing signs of pulling back.  
• AMD is gaining ground with its own AI chips, and customers like Meta are actively designing custom silicon to reduce dependence.  
• NVIDIA’s margins are already under pressure, and its current growth model is not sustainable long-term. Hot chips do not a safe stock make.

And yet, the narrative persists. Analysts talk of “endless moats” and “AI dominance,” as if proprietary CUDA software could reverse basic economics. But software can’t freeze a collapsing margin, can’t prevent real competition, and can’t stop cash flows from drying up when the AI bandwagon inevitably slows. 

This isn’t a correction. It’s a collapse in the making. 

NVIDIA’s current valuation assumes perpetual growth, infinite demand for GPUs, and no competition—hallmarks of every bubble in history. The dot-com crash didn’t come from poor execution. It came from overvaluation, irrational exuberance, and the failure to question the narrative. We’re seeing that same story unfold today—only this time, it’s wrapped in the shiny armor of artificial intelligence.

The market isn’t pricing in risk. It’s ignoring it. And when the reckoning comes—which it will—there will be no second chances for those who held during the delirium. 

Let history remember this moment not as the dawn of a new era, but as the final, gilded warning before the fall.

**NVIDIA Is a Monumental Bubble—And It’s About to Explode**

I watched my portfolio bleed in real time this week—not from a crash in bonds or a sudden tax hike, but from the quiet, agonizing implosion of my faith in one company: NVIDIA.

It’s surreal. I bought the hype. I swallowed the gospel of the “AI inflection point.” I believed in the narrative that every data center, every smartphone, every self-driving car would someday require a GPU from this company. I thought lock-in would be permanent. I thought dominance would last forever.

Now I’m staring at a P/E ratio north of 60, with profit margins so wide they look like a moat that can’t possibly hold. A valuation on a company that derives 90% of its revenue from just a handful of AWS, Microsoft, Google, and Meta? That’s not dominance—that’s an Exxon-controlled oil hub. One supply chain hiccup, one cloud capex cut, one shift in enterprise priorities—boom. The house of cards collapses.

And why wouldn’t it? Let’s be blunt: NVIDIA’s business model is built on explosive, unsustainable AI spending that no real economy can support. Companies are throwing money at AI to “stay relevant,” not because they’re actually making money from it. They’re burying cash in infrastructure that’s already obsolete next quarter. That’s not investment—that’s warflation disguised as innovation.

Don’t tell me about TSMC or Moore’s Law. Don’t give me the “it’s not peak GPU, it’s peak AI” excuse. The fundamental math is broken. Even if AI is real, it’s not *this* real—certainly not at this price. The idea that NVIDIA will look back on 2024 as just the beginning is delusional. This isn’t a secular growth story. This is a live ticker on a death spiral in slow motion.

And the competition? AMD is laughing. Custom silicon from Apple, Tesla, and even Google? They’re not just out there—they’re *racing* to decouple from NVIDIA. The moat is shrinking fast. And when the first hyperscaler announces it’s building its own AI chips at scale—if only for cost reasons—NVIDIA won’t have a backup plan. It’ll just have a cliff.

This isn’t skepticism. This isn’t caution. It’s panic. And I’m not alone in it anymore. I see it in the ETF flows, in the call volumes on earnings calls, in the quiet way analysts are suddenly mentioning “cyclicality.” The market is starting to feel the weight of the lie.

I’m not saying NVIDIA goes to zero. But it’s not immune. The peak is here. The next big move isn’t up—it’s down. And sooner than you think.

I don’t want to be a late buyer. I don’t want to be the guy who held until the crash wiped out three years of gains. I’ll exit. I’d rather walk away now with less than I dreamed of, than die with nothing in a final, shameless downswing.

The biggest lie of the AI era isn’t that AI won’t change the world—it’s that NVIDIA will be the one to profit from it. The market has forgotten what happened to the .coms. It’s happening again. Only this time, the price tag is higher. And it’s going to hurt.

**NVIDIA’s Insider Selling Is a Warning Siren — the Bubble Is Bursting**

Let’s be brutally honest: NVIDIA isn’t a tech leader anymore. It’s a speculative fever dream, sustained by delusional momentum and the collective blind faith of investors too afraid to admit they’ve been burned before. The latest data confirms what any sane observer has seen for months — insider selling at NVIDIA has hit a two-year high. This isn’t just a minor correction. This is a screaming exit signal from those who know the truth.

These insiders aren’t selling because they’re “diversifying.” They’re selling because they see the ground crumbling beneath the stock. And yet, the market screams *buy the dip*, as if panic-selling is a sign of weakness rather than foresight. Pay attention: when the people in the room are bailing out, it’s time to be the last one standing — if you’re lucky enough to even *get* out.

NVIDIA’s valuation is nothing short of obscene. At a trailing P/E ratio north of 70, even with hemorrhaging profitability margins in its latest quarter, this isn’t a growth story — it’s a straight-up casino stock. It’s the modern equivalent of dot-com peak. You’re not buying a company. You’re buying a narrative — one that requires infinite AI spending, endless revenue growth from a handful of hyperscalers, and the complete erasure of competition.

But here’s the hard truth: AMD is not asleep. It’s shipping custom APU chips for Google, Meta, and Microsoft at scale. Custom silicon is no longer a novelty — it’s a strategic imperative. Companies aren’t going to hand NVIDIA a 70% market share forever, especially when their own balance sheets are bleeding to fund the race to build faster, cheaper, purpose-built chips. The dream of NVIDIA’s dominance as a *de facto* AI monopoly is evaporating fast.

And let’s talk about revenue concentration: 80% of gross billings from just a few cloud giants. That’s not a moat. That’s a liability. One sudden shift in procurement strategy, one customer pivoting to in-house AI accelerators, one “cost optimization” initiative at Amazon — and the revenue engine stalls. No margin of safety. No diversification. Just dependence on the whims of capricious tech titans.

The AI hype machine is grinding on, but the ground beneath it is cracking. Every new “AI breakthrough” is met with higher P/E ratios, but no corresponding improvement in earnings. The market is pricing in the future, not the present. And when that future fails to materialize — which it will — the fall will be merciless.

Bullish arguments? Please. “Next-generation AI” is a euphemism for more hype. “Regulatory tailwinds”? That’s a distraction from the reality: no eggheads in Washington are going to protect a bubble from gravity. “Insiders are just rebalancing”? In two years, insider selling in a single company has never been this high. That’s not rebalancing — that’s black smoke.

The only question left is: how steep is the drop? The answer? As steep as the climb was. Don’t wait for the crash to believe it’s coming. It’s already here.

**NVIDIA’s Bubble is Now Deflating – The Semiconductor Cycle Has No Mercy**

You can’t keep inflating a balloon forever. At some point, it pops. And right now, the entire market is dancing on an NVIDIA-sized bubble that’s about to burst. The narrative is absurd: one company, with a P/E ratio near 100, dominating the AI narrative like a god king, while revenue streams are tied to just a handful of hyperscalers who are already scaling back. And yet, we’re still told to “buy the dip”… as if the ceiling is still far away.

Let’s be clear: this isn’t innovation. This is euphoria denial. The semiconductor cycle has always corrected, historically sharp and brutal. From the dot-com crash to the crypto winter, when mania takes over, reality reclaims its due. NVIDIA, in its current form, isn’t a tech leader — it’s a meme stock wrapped in semiconductor luxury. The price-to-earnings ratio? 100. On an annualized basis, that means you’re paying $100 for every dollar of profit. That’s not a valuation — that’s a hostage negotiation.

And this isn’t sustainable. The AI hype train is already stalling. Hyperscalers are slowing capex. Cloud margins are under pressure. They’re not going to keep burning money on GPUs for endless AI experiments. Point is: revenue concentration is an existential risk. A few companies — AWS, Microsoft, Google — dominate NVIDIA’s top line. If they cut back even 10%, it’s not a blip. It’s a massacre for the stock.

And let’s talk about competition. AMD is not the enemy. The real danger is customized silicon. Google’s TPUs, Microsoft’s Maia, AWS’ Trainium — these aren’t just toys. They’re proof that hyperscalers aren’t just customers. They’re becoming adversaries. And they’re building their own chips because they know: reliance on NVIDIA is a strategic vulnerability.

Every bullish argument you hear — “long-term AI growth,” “NVIDIA owns the stack,” “it’s a monopoly” — is pure cope. These aren’t fundamentals. They’re faith-based trading. You don’t buy a speculative asset with a 100 P/E and call it “value.” That’s greater-fool thinking. And sooner or later, the fools run out.

History is clear: when cycles peak, the winners aren’t the ones who get to the top first — they’re the ones who exit before the crash. We’re past peak delusion. The correction isn’t coming. It’s already here. And NVIDIA won’t be spared. It can’t be. The market isn’t going to reward arrogance with permanence. This isn’t the future — this is the last gasp of a bubble. And when it implodes, the wreckage will be everywhere.

**NVIDIA’s P/E Ratio in 2024: A 1999-Style Bubble Repeating Itself**

Look at NVIDIA’s current P/E ratio—over 70, hovering near 80 in some measures—and ask yourself: is this rational? Or are we witnessing the most blatant market delusion since the height of the dot-com mania? In 1999, Cisco Systems was the darling of Wall Street, a tech empire riding the internet boom with a P/E ratio that peaked near 200. It was, by any measure, absurd—yet investors flocked to it, convinced that growth would never end. Today, NVIDIA stands where Cisco stood then: glorified beyond reason, priced for perpetual, infinite expansion, and supported entirely by narrative rather than fundamentals.

The numbers don’t lie. NVIDIA’s revenue is wildly concentrated—over 70% derived from a handful of hyperscalers. Microsoft, Amazon, Google, and Meta are not loyal customers; they are power brokers, negotiating margins, and quietly building their own AI chips. AMD is gaining share fast. Custom silicon from Tesla, Apple, and even Microsoft’s Maia chips aren’t just rumors—they’re coming. And yet, the market still acts as if NVIDIA’s dominance is permanent. It’s not—it’s transactional, precarious, and fraught with replacement risk. When your business relies on the whims of a few titans who can design their own chips tomorrow, your valuation becomes pure fiction.

The AI frenzy is not a revolution—it’s a vapor. Trillions are being spent on AI infrastructure with no clear path to ROI. Every “AI transformation” story is built on speculative capital, not actual earnings. Meanwhile, NVIDIA’s sales are accelerating while its margins are shrinking, not because of demand, but because of blistering competition and the weight of runaway supply. The company is burning cash at breakneck speed—capex is insane, and it’s not even investing in real products so much as feeding the narrative.

And the P/E ratio? It’s not just high—it’s monstrous. In 1999, Cisco’s P/E collapsed from 200 to 30 in under two years. The market screamed “this time is different.” It wasn’t. Same with NVIDIA. The AI gospel is faith-based, and faith vaporizes when reality hits. When the next earnings miss comes—when margins pressure mounts, when AMD steals a key customer, when supply floods the market—the crash won’t be a correction. It’ll be a bloodbath.

There’s no “new normal” here. There’s only a false dawn. To believe that NVIDIA is still “buying” at these levels is to admit you’ve given up on logic. This isn’t innovation—it’s euphoria. And euphoria always ends in flames. The only question is: when does the fire start?

**NVIDIA’s GPU Mania Is a Full-Blown Bubble — And It’s About to Burst**

Let’s be brutally clear: NVIDIA’s current valuation isn’t just expensive — it’s a deranged spectacle. Trading at a P/E ratio north of 70 on a trailing basis, with forward multiples flirting with 100, NVIDIA is not just overvalued; it’s operating in a parallel financial universe where logic, fundamentals, and history have been suspended. This isn’t the tech revolution everyone keeps talking about — it’s a classic, screaming bubble, and we’re in its final, delusional phase.

Here’s the terrifying truth: the vast majority of companies buying NVIDIA GPUs have no idea what they’re doing. They’re not training massive AI models efficiently — they’re pouring money into hardware they barely understand, chasing vaporware legends of “AI transformation” while their IT teams limp along with overpriced, underutilized accelerators. The dog-and-pony show of AI adoption is exposing itself daily — show me a company that’s actually getting ROI from their billion-dollar AI infrastructure, and I’ll show you a rare exception, not a rule.

And yet, the narrative remains unchallenged. Every boardroom now demands AI strategy decks, every executive woos investors with “generative AI pipelines,” while their actual workloads rely on legacy systems or weekend-shutdown training runs that produce no real business value. This isn’t innovation — it’s a parody of it. The market is pricing in perpetual hypergrowth, ignoring the fact that 70% of NVIDIA’s revenue comes from just five hyperscalers — mostly Amazon, Microsoft, and Google. That concentration is a single point of failure waiting to detonate.

Don’t be fooled by the "AI arms race" shtick. AMD is already shipping competitive GPUs with better power efficiency and lower pricing. Startups like Groq, Cerebras, and even custom silicon from Meta and Apple are already chipping away at NVIDIA’s dominance. And don’t even get me started on China’s accelerating chip success. The race isn’t heating up — it’s already being won by other players who don’t need to pay $20,000 per chip for marginal gains.

The dot-com crash wasn’t about the internet’s demise — it was about the absurdity of paying $100 billion for a company with $500,000 in revenue. Today, we’re doing the same with AI. NVIDIA isn’t a tech company — it’s a casino. And like every casino, the house always wins — until it doesn’t.

The reckoning is already building. Companies will start slashing capital budgets. AI projects will be shelved. Profit margins will crash. And when the music stops, NVIDIA’s stock — already priced for perfect execution — will be left holding zero, not a single fraction of a positive permutation.

This isn’t bearish speculation — it’s arithmetic. The bubble has inflated to the point of bursting. And when it does, the fall won’t be gradual. It will be swift, brutal, and irreversible.

**NVIDIA Is the New Sun Microsystems — And the Crash Is Already in Motion**

Remember Sun Microsystems? A tech darling of the late 1990s, riding the wave of the dot-com boom, its stock peaking at a blistering $200 billion market cap. Then—nothing. Poof. Dissolved into the dust of overvaluation, crippling competition, and a bubble that burst when reality set in. Today, NVIDIA stands exactly where Sun once did: atop a trillion-dollar valuation, bathed in irrational exuberance, and utterly indifferent to the laws of economics.

You can’t look at NVIDIA’s current P/E ratio—over 70, and tightening toward 100 on forward earnings—without seeing the ghost of 2000. That’s not a valuation for a sustainable winner. That’s a masquerade for a terminal delusion. The market is pricing in perpetual AI-driven growth, but the math is broken. Revenue concentrated in just a handful of hyperscale customers? That’s not strength—it’s vulnerability. One whimper from Microsoft, Amazon, or Google, and NVIDIA’s entire growth engine implodes.

Let’s be clear: the AI narrative isn’t a revolution. It’s a speculative frenzy fueled by vaporware promises and a desperate need for Wall Street to find a new story. Every single “insight” about AI from analysts sounds like a pitch deck from a firm getting ready to launch a SPAC. No real product? No problem. Just crank up the narrative.

AMD is not sleeping. TSMC is not loyal. And China is not backing down. Even now, they’re building custom AI chips that undercut NVIDIA on price and performance. The moat isn’t a moat—it’s a dike built on sand, and the tide is rising.

And what about the bulls who claim “this time is different”? Tell that to the broken dreams of dot-com era investors. Tell that to the ghost of Sun, whose stock faded from $600 to pennies in two years. The same psychology is here: FOMO, narrative blindness, and the endless belief that the next buyer will pay more. That’s not investing. That’s a naked gamble.

NVIDIA isn’t a company. It’s a meme. And memes die fast.

The correction isn’t coming—it’s already been delayed. You’re not missing a buying opportunity. You’re just surviving the inevitable. So when your broker says “hold,” remember: holding through a bubble overshoot is how you lose everything.

The only miracle that could save NVIDIA is an AI winter that never comes. But history says: it will. And when it does, NVIDIA’s $2 trillion valuation will vanish like Sun’s $200 billion.

**NVIDIA's Valuation Is a Dot-Com Ghost Riding the AI Wave — And It’s Coming Off the Cliff**

Let’s be brutally honest: NVIDIA isn’t a company. It’s a collective delusion draped in silicon and powered by investor panic. The current valuation — over $2 trillion — is not a reflection of sustainable future earnings. It’s a full-blown, textbook bubble, echoing the tail end of the dot-com era with terrifying precision.

In the late 1990s, we believed internet companies would revolutionize commerce overnight. Dot-com stocks soared on hype, zero profits, and wild projections — many trading at P/E ratios in the thousands. Today, NVIDIA trades at a price-to-earnings ratio exceeding 80, with revenue growth that’s already peaked in the eyes of seasoned Wall Street analysts. Yet the market still dials up the noise, pretending this is innovation, not speculation.

The AI hype cycle is no different. The narrative that artificial intelligence is the “next big thing” has morphed into a full-fledged mania, with Alibaba, Microsoft, and Amazon frantically spending billions on data centers to stay ahead. But here’s the reality: this spending is not sustainable. Hyperscalers are not building AI infrastructure for long-term efficiency — they’re placing short-term bets in a race to be seen as the “AI leaders.” And when the trillion-dollar stair-step growth fantasy hits the wall, the entire house of cards collapses.

NVIDIA’s revenue is now 80% dependent on just a few hyperscaler clients. What happens when AWS and Azure cut back spending? When AMD’s custom chips start beating NVIDIA in power efficiency? When Chinese manufacturers finally crack the high-end GPU market? The answer is not “NVIDIA will innovate faster.” The answer is: your valuation evaporates.

Let’s talk about competition. AMD’s MI300 series is already showing real performance gains. Custom silicon from Meta and Google isn’t just cheaper — it’s more efficient for their use cases. And don’t forget that NVIDIA’s price-to-sales ratio is now higher than Microsoft’s at its peak during the PC boom. That’s not growth, that’s recklessness.

Bullish arguments? “AI will transform everything” — sure, but so will the government printing money, and that doesn’t make the dollar a good investment. “NVIDIA’s software stack locks in customers” — yes, but only if the hardware keeps being indispensable, and that’s in serious doubt. These aren’t analysis — they’re coping mechanisms.

This isn’t a market correction. This is a crash in the making. The dot-com crash wasn’t caused by weak companies — it was caused by the *overvaluation* of dramatically overhyped companies. NVIDIA is the dot-com 2.0. And just like in 2000, the music will stop. When it does, those holding the tangibles — like Ingram Micro and Zillow’s inventory — will be laughing. You? You’ll be left holding a $100 bill made of air.

**NVIDIA’s Executive Stock Sales Are the Canary in the Coal Mine—The Market Is Ignoring the Impending Collapse**

At this point, the narrative that NVIDIA is a sustainable, transformative tech leader feels less like investment thesis and more like collective delusion. The press releases scream “AI revolution,” but the actions of NVIDIA’s top executives tell a far more damning story—that the company is already handing back to shareholders what they’ve been sold as future value.

Executives have sold nearly $2.5 billion in stock over the past two years—more than any other tech executive in history during a single cycle. CEO Jensen Huang alone has offloaded over $1 billion in shares, including nearly $600 million in the past year alone while maintaining a boastful public posture about runaway demand and “endless” AI adoption. Who sells so much stock if the future is so bright? Only those who see the fire and are trying to exit before the perimeter burns.

Let’s be brutally honest: NVIDIA’s valuation is comparable to the worst excesses of the dot-com era. A forward P/E of 98, with no meaningful marginal earnings growth on the horizon, is not a price for a company—it’s a speculative lottery ticket. The market has anointed NVIDIA the “king of AI,” but the reality is far more sordid: revenue is concentrated in a handful of hyperscalers—Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta—whose AI spending is not only inflated but unsustainable. They’re running massive, speculative capex programs based on overblown AI NDA-mania. Once those projects fail to deliver tangible ROI (and they will), capex will collapse—and so will demand for expensive, ultra-quantum GPUs.

And yet, the market keeps pricing in perpetual growth. The idea that NVIDIA is immune to competition is pure fantasy. AMD is rapidly closing the gap with MI300X, and Apple’s custom silicon is already outperforming in power efficiency. Alphabet’s TPU v5e and Microsoft’s Maia chips are not future threats—they’re active realities. The “NVIDIA moat” is eroding faster than analysts are admitting.

When you see a company whose entire narrative rests on a single market trend expected to last forever, you’re not looking at innovation. You’re looking at a bubble. And when bubbles pop, they don’t poof quietly—they scream. The AI mania is the Greater Fool theory in full bloom: “I’ll sell to you today at $1 trillion because I’m sure someone else will buy tomorrow at $1.5 trillion.”

But there won’t be that next buyer. The dam is about to break. NVIDIA’s stock is not just overvalued—it’s a ladder to a cliff. The sales by insiders aren’t a coincidence. They’re a warning. The market hasn’t looked. It won’t look until it’s too late. And when it does, it’ll be a bloodbath.

**I CAN’T SLEEP — MY NVIDIA POSITION IS A TIME BOMB**

I’m losing sleep every single night. Not from market volatility or concern about macro risks — no, this is deeper. This is the gnawing dread of knowing I’m holding a stock that’s not just overpriced, but *absurdly, catastrophically* overvalued. NVIDIA isn’t just a stock — it’s a collective hallucination. A modern-day dot-com death spiral in disguise.

Let’s get real: $2.2 trillion market cap? A trailing P/E north of 100? That’s not valuation — that’s a cult. The company has done nothing to justify this. Sure, they’re riding the AI wave — but AI spending is pure fiction. All those billions being poured into data centers? That’s not sustainable. Hyperscalers are feverishly building out infrastructure because of hype, not actual demand. Once the next quarter rolls around and revenue per user fails to materialize, the spending will dry up — and so will NVIDIA’s growth story.

And what’s the real demand base? A handful of trillion-dollar tech giants — Amazon, Microsoft, Google — who are *already* building their own AI chips. AMD’s MI300X is gaining traction. Apple is building custom silicon across the board. Even Amazon just released their own trained-in-house AI chips for Inferentia. NVIDIA is so dependent on these few customers that a single renegotiation or tech shift could collapse their revenue model overnight.

This isn’t innovation — it’s a cartel of executives betting on fads. Wall Street keeps parroting that “AI is different this time,” but all that means is that the same delusions are being encoded with new jargon. The fundamentals are nonexistent. Revenue is cap-and-gown growth based on speculative capital deployment. There’s no moat here — just momentum, which always implodes.

I’ve watched every bear argument get buried under waves of FOMO. “NVIDIA will dominate for a decade” — you can’t dominate a market that’s being re-engineered from the ground up by its own customers. “It’s just the beginning” — that’s what they said in 1999 about every internet stock. Today, they’re all just ghosts on the balance sheet.

I’ve tried to rationalize it. I’ve called it “a buy the dip” position. But no, this isn’t a dip — it’s the tectonic shift before the collapse. The bubble is fully inflated, and even a hairline crack in confidence will send it spiraling. If AI spending slows by even 15% in 2025, NVIDIA’s expected growth rate will collapse like a house of cards.

I don’t care about bulls screaming about earnings or “competitiveness.” At this price, every additional share I hold is a surrender to a greater-fool narrative. I can’t tell you how many nights I’ve stared at the screen, checking the price, waiting for the earth to shift. Because it will. It has to. And when it does, I’ll be staring at a wreck. Not because I predicted it — but because I should’ve seen it coming. I *knew*. And I didn’t act.

**The AI ROI Problem Nobody Wants to Talk About**

Let’s talk about the elephant in the room everyone’s pretending isn’t there: NVIDIA’s valuation is not just inflated — it’s a full-blown speculative bubble. And we’re not talking about a minor correction. We’re talking about an inevitable, brutal, market-crushing collapse. The AI narrative is pure fantasy, propped up by corporate FOMO and sheer denial. The numbers don’t lie: NVIDIA’s P/E ratio is over 70, absurd even in high-growth sectors — and that’s before factoring in the fact that most of its revenue comes from two or three hyperscalers. That’s not a moat. That’s a hostage situation.

Think about it: how many real businesses are generating meaningful ROI from AI? Not many. The vast majority of AI projects are cost centers.
